message.content:
The title of “best jazz singer” is highly subjective and varies depending on personal taste, era, and style. However, several artists are frequently cited as the most influential and celebrated jazz vocalists:

| Artist | Notable Contributions | Why They’re Often Mentioned |
|--------|-----------------------|-----------------------------|
| **Billie Holiday** | Pioneered a deeply emotive, improvisational vocal style. | Her phrasing and emotional depth set a new standard for jazz singing. |
| **Ella Fitzgerald** | Known as the “First Lady of Song,” she mastered scat singing and flawless diction. | Her technical mastery and versatility made her a benchmark for vocal excellence. |
| **Sarah Vaughan** | Possessed a rich, operatic voice with incredible range and control. | Her blend of jazz, blues, and pop showcased unmatched vocal artistry. |
| **Nat King Cole** | Combined smooth jazz phrasing with a warm, conversational tone. | His crossover appeal and lyrical delivery made him a household name. |
| **Cassandra Wilson** | Blends jazz with folk, blues, and world music. | Her innovative approach and deep, resonant voice keep her at the forefront of contemporary jazz. |

If you’re looking for a definitive “best” pick, many critics and fans still point to **Billie Holiday** as the most iconic and transformative jazz vocalist of all time. However, the genre’s richness means there’s always room for new voices to rise and redefine what “best” can mean.
